text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Paging spike detected for inference-runtime (svc-prefix-cache). Severity: P1. Triggered 1787654321. Auto-paging to oncall.
jamal: got the page, I'm on it. pinging eng-runtime and eng-sre.
sarah: seeing huge KV prefix-key growth right after the template-render rollout at ~02:01 UTC. mem pressure on inference nodes spiking, OOMs on 2 workers.
miguel: metrics snapshot:
```
kv_prefix_keys_per_host: 120k -> 4.8M
inference_batch_queue_size p95: 12 -> 430
generate_latency_p95: 180ms -> 1.8s
swap_used: +18GB on worker-3
```
miguel: logs show "batch queue overflow" and lots of duplicate prefix keys (same prompt variants hashing to different bins).
jamal: @sarah can you confirm whether the new prompt templating change touched tokenizer outputs? that could explain different hash inputs.
sarah: template change introduced a thin whitespace normalization step in the client-libs; looks like it produced different tokenization in some edge templates. noticed mismatch between tokenizer v1.3 (prod) and v1.4 (canary) in a few samples.
oncall-bot: Next rotation: @eva will take escalation in ~9 minutes.
jamal: immediate mitigation: disabling continuous batching on canary pool to reduce queue buildup while we triage. running:
```
rgctl set pool.canary.batching.enabled=false --reason "mitigate kv cache blowup"
```
sarah: confirm: batching disabled on canary nodes. batch queues draining now. latency p95 down to ~420ms but throughput down ~35%.
miguel: pushing eviction temp-policy to KV cache to aggressively GC prompt prefixes older than 1h:
```
kvctl set policy prefix_cache ttl=3600 --scope=inference
```
miguel: eviction running, estimated reclaimed keys ~3.2M across cluster. paging IO dropping.
linda (support): initial customer impact: reported tickets: CS-9821, CS-9823, CS-9826 - customers AICorp, BrightDocs, QueryFlow saw increased latencies and a few timeouts. notifying them now with interim status.
jamal: patch identified: tokenizer normalization mismatch caused inconsistent hash input; PR #4321 normalizes on-model-side before hashing and pins tokenizer to stable v1.3 for now. prepping canary deploy for that patch.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: jamal initiated rollout (canary 2 nodes) - PR 4321.
jamal: canary logs look good after patch: duplicate-key rate dropping, kv_prefix_keys_per_host trending down, mem usage stabilizing on canary nodes.
miguel: paging stopped on canary, overall paging IOPS falling to baseline. continuing rollout to remaining nodes in waves of 5.
support-bot: customer notifications sent: "We're mitigating a latency incident affecting inference results, temporary throttles applied; expecting recovery in <2h>." (message id: msg-9876)
jamal: rolling patch to all inference nodes now. monitoring for regressions. keeping batching disabled until we see stable key counts and tokenization consistency.
eva: taking over handoff @jamal - summary: root cause is tokenizer mismatch from templating change -> inconsistent prefix hashing -> kv cache blowup -> batching queue saturation -> paging. Current state:
- Patch PR #4321 rolled to all nodes (in progress)
- Batching disabled on canary; will re-enable only after metrics check
- Eviction TTL set to 1h and ran successfully
- Customers notified; CS tickets being tracked
Plan: finish rollout, validate metrics for 30m, re-enable batching in canary, then ramp.
jamal: additional mitigation we applied: temporary rate-limit for non-priority tenants to reduce write amplification to KV cache:
```
rgctl set rate-limit write_per_minute=200 --selector="tier!=enterprise"
```
linda: noted impact: three major customers saw 3-6% error rates on generate calls during the spike window (02:00-02:25 UTC). support team will follow up with credits where appropriate.
jamal: runbook TODOs (for postmortem):
- pin tokenizer versions in rollout CI
- add unit test for whitespace normalization -> tokenization invariants
- alert: kv_cache_keys_per_host > 1M delta in 5m
- add canary gating for prompt-templating changes
- evaluate safer default for continuous batching (thresholds)
- schedule customer follow-ups and postmortem writeup
sarah: I'll open follow-up PRs for CI pins and add tests. ETA EOD.
eva: I'll own postmortem and customer timeline. taking full responsibility for next 24h handoff.
incident-bot: Severity changed: P1 -> P2 at 1787654590 (mitigations successful, customer impact contained).
jamal: handoff notes posted to #incidents-runbook, linking to logs and dashboards. last check: kv keys stable ~95k per host, generate_latency_p95 ~220ms.
eva: taking primary. if anyone sees re-escalation pings, page me directly @eva. closing active paging for now; will keep monitoring.
jamal: thanks team. handoff complete.
